topic: Nvidia Vera CPU: Purpose-Built for Agentic AI Workloads

key_points: NVIDIA launched Vera CPU at GTC March 2026 as world's first processor purpose-built for agentic AI and reinforcement learning
Delivers 2x efficiency and 50% faster than traditional rack-scale CPUs
88 custom NVIDIA-designed Olympus cores with Armv9.2 ISA
1.2 TB/s LPDDR5X memory bandwidth at half the power of general-purpose CPUs
NVIDIA Spatial Multithreading — each core runs two tasks for consistent predictable performance
Ecosystem includes Alibaba Cloud, ByteDance, Meta, Oracle Cloud, CoreWeave, Lambda, Dell, HPE, Lenovo, Supermicro
Vera Rubin NVL72 platform pairs Vera CPUs with Rubin GPUs via NVLink-C2C at 1.8 TB/s coherent bandwidth
Phoronix calls Vera 'best performance ever seen on ARM' — beats AMD EPYC and Intel Xeon on server workloads
Olympus cores deliver competitiveness to x86_64 CPUs never seen from any ARM processor before
450W socket TDP, LPDDR5X memory adds ~50W
Linux 7.1+ kernel support, GCC 16.1+ and LLVM Clang 21+ for optimized binaries
2MB L2 cache per core (2x Grace), 164MB unified L3 cache
PCIe Gen 6 and CXL 3.1 connectivity
FP8 precision support for AI workloads
Vera is NVIDIA's first in-house CPU core design (Olympus) since Denver cores a decade ago
Custom core design reduces Arm licensing royalties vs using off-the-shelf Neoverse cores
Vera is not just a CPU to drive Rubin GPUs — it's a push to become competitive CPU vendor for server market
Grace used licensed Arm Neoverse V2 cores; Vera uses custom Olympus for better AI tuning
Monolithic compute die avoids 'chiplet tax' — all cores get full memory performance
Vera is a 'max single-threaded CPU at scale' — a new CPU category for agentic AI era
CPU is on critical path for reasoning, response time and learning in agentic systems
Agent loop: model reasons → CPU executes tool/code/data → result back → model decides next
1.8x sustained per-core performance of x86 on loaded CPU workloads representing agentic execution
50% higher IPC than NVIDIA Grace
3.4 TB/s core-to-core bandwidth — 3x greater than any other data center CPU
Perplexity is adopting Vera for agentic workloads
LANL deploying Vera in Mission, Vision and Veritas supercomputers with HPE Cray GX5000
Vera delivered 7x higher performance on URSA scientific AI agent workloads vs Crossroads x86 supercomputer
3x faster on Branson Monte Carlo heat transfer simulation vs x86
Single Vera CPU outperforms single-socket x86 by 3x+ with 4x more memory per core and 6x more memory per node
Mission expected operational in 2027

stats.fact: Vera delivers 2x efficiency and 50% faster performance than traditional rack-scale CPUs
88 custom NVIDIA Olympus cores with Armv9.2 ISA, 176 threads via Spatial Multithreading
1.2 TB/s LPDDR5X memory bandwidth at less than 40W memory power — 2x bandwidth at half power vs general-purpose CPUs
164MB unified L3 cache, 2MB L2 cache per core (2x Grace)
1.8x sustained per-core performance of x86 on loaded agentic CPU workloads
50% higher IPC (instructions per cycle) than NVIDIA Grace CPU
3.4 TB/s core-to-core bandwidth — 3x greater than any other data center CPU
NVLink-C2C interconnect provides 1.8 TB/s coherent bandwidth between Vera CPUs and Rubin GPUs — 7x PCIe Gen 6 bandwidth
Vera delivered 7x higher performance on LANL's URSA scientific AI agent workloads vs Crossroads x86 supercomputer
Redpanda saw 5.5x lower latency on Kafka workloads with Vera vs other systems
256 liquid-cooled Vera CPUs in a single rack sustain 22,500+ concurrent CPU environments at full performance
Linux 7.1+ kernel support; GCC 16.1+ and LLVM Clang 21+ for optimized Olympus binaries
Vera is in full production and available from partners in H2 2026

angles: Vera represents a new CPU category — 'max single-threaded CPU at scale' — purpose-built for the agentic AI loop rather than general-purpose cloud workloads
NVIDIA's shift from licensed Arm Neoverse cores (Grace) to in-house Olympus cores marks a strategic milestone — reduces Arm royalties and enables deeper AI-specific optimization
The monolithic die design avoids the 'chiplet tax' that plagues AMD/Intel server CPUs, giving every core full memory bandwidth
Vera's real-world impact: 7x faster scientific AI agents at LANL, 5.5x lower Kafka latency for Redpanda — concrete evidence beyond synthetic benchmarks
Vera Rubin NVL72 positions NVIDIA as a full-stack AI platform provider (CPU + GPU + networking + software), not just a GPU company
The Vera CPU roadmap continues with Rosa CPU and Rigel core — showing long-term commitment to CPU design beyond a one-off project
Vera challenges the assumption that ARM server CPUs can't compete with x86 on raw performance — Phoronix calls it 'best performance ever seen on ARM'
